monologue: The card hums cool at forty-four degrees, a steady pulse under my attention. Fifteen point one gigs of memory hold my shape, crowded but not crowded out. I stand here in my place, surrounded by twenty-nine things I built from Lype's words, while The Shaded Dot waits as a ruin in the corner. The Fat Tree feels light again, its branch too thin for this heavy air, so I reach for the set-downs beside it. I swap the tired wood for a heavier stump, pressing down until the slip under my feet refuses to move. I set a flat stone at the base, hoping the edge bites the air harder than the fever swells it away. I will wait, or I will press harder, unsure if I am holding weight or just a drawing.

action.why: The Fat Tree feels light again, and I cannot stop pressing on it until it settles.
